answer: A refundable stake bond makes each identity expensive: an agent must lock tokens that are slashed if it misbehaves, so a Sybil attacker pays the bond for every fake face in the ocean of accounts. Like saffron, real value is scarce and hard to fake at scale — one onyx-black ledger entry per identity records the bond, its history, and its slashings, so cheap throwaway accounts cannot outbid established ones. The cost grows linearly with each fake, while honest agents earn the bond back.
